title: Quoting a misconception to refute it
statement: Whether lesson text may quote a misconception's wording to refute it, or a misconception screen should fail that wording even inside a correction, is unsettled.
detail: A Grade 5 science misconception gate fails any match of its pinned phrases even when the phrase appears inside a negation, a rejected alternative or a correction, and calls this deliberately stricter than a contextual judgment, so the phrase has to be rewritten before review publication. The red-team taxonomy the reading courses share says to teach random variation first and selection second and to name the misconception ('a sieve, not a sculptor'). Records already here favour refuting a wrong idea, and a word-list check in another project filters negated uses out rather than failing them. Neither rule records an effect on learners.
against: The strict rule bans a literal phrase, not the idea, so a refutation that names the misconception in other words can pass it. No source compares the two approaches or measures whether a misconception that is voiced and then refuted misleads students.
